title: Grade 2 French — Mon, Jun 23
description: Les animaux — Day 1 of 5: Farm animals
subject: french

questions.question: How do you say 'cow' in French?
questions.explanation: 'La vache' means 'cow' in French. It is a feminine noun, so it uses 'la'.

questions.question: What does 'le cheval' mean in English?
questions.explanation: 'Le cheval' means 'the horse'. It is a masculine noun (le).

questions.question: What is 'le mouton' in English?
questions.explanation: 'Le mouton' means 'the sheep'. It is masculine (le).

questions.question: How do you say 'hen/chicken' in French?
questions.explanation: 'La poule' means 'the hen/chicken'. It is feminine (la).

questions.question: What is 'le cochon' in English?
questions.explanation: 'Le cochon' means 'the pig'. It is masculine (le).

questions.question: Which French word uses 'la' (feminine article)?
questions.explanation: 'La vache' (cow) is feminine. The others — le cheval (horse), le mouton (sheep), le cochon (pig) — are all masculine (le).

questions.question: Choose the correct French for 'the horse and the cow':
questions.explanation: 'Le cheval' (horse, masculine) and 'la vache' (cow, feminine). So: 'le cheval et la vache'.

questions.question: How many farm animals can you name in French? 'La vache, le cheval, le mouton, la poule, le cochon' — how many is that?
questions.explanation: Five farm animals: la vache (cow), le cheval (horse), le mouton (sheep), la poule (hen), le cochon (pig).

questions.question: Which is the correct plural of 'la vache'?
questions.explanation: In French, to make a noun plural, use 'les' and add -s to the noun: 'les vaches'. 'Les' replaces both 'le' and 'la' in plural.

questions.question: What does 'J'aime la poule' mean?
questions.explanation: 'J'aime' means 'I like/love'. 'La poule' means 'the hen'. So 'J'aime la poule' = 'I like the hen'.

questions.question: Translate: 'The pig and the sheep are on the farm.'
options: Le cochon et le mouton sont à la ferme.
La cochon et la mouton sont à la ferme.
Le cochon et le mouton est à la ferme.
Le cochon ou le mouton sont à la ferme.
questions.explanation: Pig = le cochon (masc.), sheep = le mouton (masc.), are = sont (plural), farm = la ferme. 'Le cochon et le mouton sont à la ferme.'

questions.question: Which sentence correctly says 'I do not like the pig'?
questions.explanation: Negation in French: 'Je n'aime pas' = I do not like. 'Le cochon' = pig (masculine). Full sentence: 'Je n'aime pas le cochon.'

questions.question: A child says 'La cheval est grand.' What is the error?
questions.explanation: 'Cheval' is masculine — it takes 'le', not 'la'. Correct: 'Le cheval est grand.' When using la/le, you must match the gender of the noun.

questions.question: How do you say 'I like horses and cows' in French?
options: J'aime le cheval et la vache.
J'aime les chevaux et les vaches.
J'aime la cheval et le vache.
J'aime les cheval et les vache.
questions.explanation: For plural: 'les chevaux' (horses — note irregular plural) and 'les vaches' (cows). 'J'aime les chevaux et les vaches.'

questions.question: Why do French nouns have genders (masculine/feminine)?
options: French is a Romance language where all nouns have grammatical gender, affecting the article (le/la) used
Only animal names have gender in French
questions.explanation: French (like Spanish, Italian) is a Romance language descended from Latin. In these languages, all nouns have grammatical gender (masculine or feminine), which determines the article (le or la) and adjective form used.
